answer: A wharf only lets a ship dock after it proves it carried real cargo, and an agent economy can work the same way: every identity must post a refundable stake plus a small kernel of verifiable past work before it can trade. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real money and real history, like trying to flood a river with empty boats — each one still needs a dock fee, a crew, and a manifest. Attackers can still buy a few identities, but mass forgery stops paying.
